neighbours.label: finite ' reads' or ' drew' straight after a noun-phrase subject
fire: The latest novel by that author reads like a diary.
Her short guide to Roman law reads very smoothly.
The report from the audit team reads as a warning.
This history of the railway reads well throughout.
The parade through the old town drew loud cheers.
The strike at the steel plant drew wide support.
Her talk on deep sea fishing drew a big audience.
The sale of the old harbour drew many complaints.
quiet: The latest novel by that author sits on my desk.
Her short guide to Roman law costs very little.
The report from the audit team came as a warning.
This history of the railway ends in 1950.
The parade through the old town began at noon.
The strike at the steel plant lasted two weeks.
Her talk on deep sea fishing ran a bit long.
The sale of the old harbour closed in June.

notes: The card's other main verbs did not generalise: ' represents' stayed at or below 0.11 in probes. 'He reads' also fired (0.28), so the subject may not matter.
